next_step: Closed-lost: reconvene in Q2 for potential migration/optimization conversation
loss_reason: Selected hyperscaler-managed endpoints (AWS) due to existing enterprise discount/EDP, tighter integration with internal IAM/KMS, and security team comfort. No internal champion to push additional procurement complexity; also budget reallocation to cloud consolidation.
notes:
Top-line: Closed-lost to AWS-managed endpoints (SageMaker/Endpoint-backed solution). Heavy on infra consolidation.

Initial thesis:
- Advanced personalization + real-time reranking for storefront and recommendation microservices.
- Need sub-50ms p95 inference for personalization calls; high throughput (2000 reqs/s steady peak).
- Strong data residency + KMS-in-HSM requirement from security.

POC summary:
- May–Aug 2024: POC with Redwood Dedicated (2x A100 equivalent), integrated KV cache demo, batch vs streaming cost analysis. SE (Carlos) ran latency sweeps; dedicated configs met p95 targets in lab.
- Security review: requested SOC2 + KMS key import options, audit log format, and longer retention. Shared security FAQ (drive:/security/solstice_security_questions.xlsx).
- Finance/procurement: asked for EDP-style pricing; we proposed committed reserved capacity model.

Signals of stall:
- Aug 2024: Procurement pushed for cloud consolidation clause — preferred vendor = existing hyperscaler (AWS) to simplify contracts and apply EDP credits.
- Sep 2024: Security team issued new guidance: use managed endpoints where possible if they integrate with org IAM and central KMS.
- Sep 30 2024: Internal re-org — original champion (Dir. ML Platforms) left; no replacement identified.

Final decision and why we lost:
- Quote from Head of Infra: "We have to consolidate on one cloud provider — the math favors AWS once EDP and migration ops are included."
- AWS offered managed endpoints with SSO/IAM integration, customer-managed KMS, and migration support via partner program; procurement favored lower perceived operational overhead.
- Security accepted hyperscaler solution after an internal gating checklist — eliminated need to negotiate custom KMS onboarding with us.

What we tried:
- Presented rollout plan with canary and fallback policies, added cost-optimizations via Redwood Optimize, and pushed for a dedicated pilot with guardrails.
- Offered security deep-dive call with engineering leadership (Carlos + Eleanor) — happened 2024-09-21 (ff_2024-09-21_exec_brief).
- Pricing: matched many line items, but could not match EDP/enterprise discount mechanics and single-vendor policy.

Follow-ups and open threads:
- Procurement confirmed deal with AWS on 2024-10-05 (internal note).
- Action: nurture for Q2 next year — angle: migration tooling, multi-cloud fallback, or cost-optimization where Redwood adds value once they hit cost/regret thresholds.
- Suggested touchpoints: platform engineering head (TBD), cloud economics team.

Internal AEs notes / coachable items:
- Need earlier exec-level sponsorship — engage CFO/Head of Cloud early when EDP is in scope.
- Prepare a clear EDP-compsheet showing how Redwood integrates into existing cloud EDP models and partner credits.
- Provide a templated security KMS onboarding playbook to reduce perceived vendor-management friction.

Stuck items / blockers (short):
- "No internal champion after re-org"
- "Procurement lock to hyperscaler for EDP"
- "Security comfortable with hyperscaler-managed endpoints"
- Budget reallocated to consolidated cloud spend

Recommended next steps (short):
- Add to Q2 chase list for 2025; refresh ROI with measured POC metrics (latency/cost) vs managed endpoints.
- Product: build one-pager on KMS import/playbook and partner EDP compatibility.
- Sales: maintain relationship, light-touch quarterly check-ins.
